nodes.title: Revisions
nodes.body:
4/4/94.  Ron E. Brockmeyer; Harbor Branch Oceanographic Institution

Common Name: Sheepshead minnow
Scientific Name: Cyprinodon variegatus

Other Common Names - Variegated minnow (306); Sheepshead killifish (279); Sheepshead pupfish (54); broad killifish, and chubby (70).

nodes.title: Classification
nodes.body:
Phylum:  Chordata
	Class:  Osteichthyes
	Order:  Atheriniformes
	Family:  Cyprinodontidae

Note: A reference for Order =  (607 608)

nodes.title: VALUE & STATUS
nodes.body:
Commercial:  Some commercial value as bait (657 554).  Statistics of their use are unknown as no records are kept.
Recreational: This species has no recreational value other than its use as bait by fishermen.
Indicator: Used extensively as a bioassay organism by United States Environmental Protection Agency and others for acute, partial chronic, and chronic bioassays necessary for setting water quality standards.  Testing is primarily for effects of organochlorides on the estuarine community, but recent work has indicated this species is useful in the evaluation of the hepatocarcinogenic risks of chemicals in contaminated coastal waters (148 240 629 628).
Ecological Role: The sheepshead minnow and other cyprinodontids are important in the control of salt water mosquitoes (306 279) and also in the export of energy from the marsh by serving as food for birds and larger fish (306 651 554).  It was the dominant species in both abundance and biomass found in IRL impounded wetlands (948).  Piscine predators include: Centropomus undecimalis, Morone interrupta, Cynoscion nebulosus, Micropogonias undulatus, Elops saurus, Megalops atlanticus, and Sciaenops ocellata (163 235 255 1026 1374).

nodes.title: GEOGRAPHIC RANGE
nodes.body:
Overall:  Along the Atlantic coast, from Maine to Yucatan, Mexico, and throughout West Indies to northern South America (54 327 275).
Within Study Area:  Throughout Florida in shallow peripheral waters (953 848 790 581 664).

Mobility and Migration:

nodes.title: Life Mode
nodes.body:
This euryhaline, oviparous, detrital-algavore feeds at the bottom in shallow open peripheral areas (279 281 953 848 790 581 664).  Markedly diurnal (Breder 1959 611); has been observed to school especially when frightened (312 437); nektonic in shallow coastal/inland waters (582  279 664 702).  Males defend breeding territories and the demersal eggs layed there (393 628 275 Kodric-Brown 1977, 1978; Raney et al. 1953).
Movements and Migrations:  Observed movements of this species appear to be influenced by seasonal fluctuations in temperature.  As temperatures begin to drop in the fall there is a general movement to warmer, slightly deeper waters.  It has been noted that at this time sheepshead minnows can be taken by trawls in these deeper waters where none were present during warmer months (70 255 657).

nodes.title: BENTHIC HABITAT
nodes.body:
Habitat Type: All stages are estuarine: restricted to bays and inland areas preferring shallow bottom, quiet waters; found in salt marshes, sloughs, coves, bays, creeks, and ditches (70 224 262 263 312 437 657 682).  Larval specimens often occupy the water's edge while larger individuals (7mm) may stay on the bottom (754).  Take advantage of mosquito control practices in wetlands associated with the IRL to spread across artificially flooded high marsh habitat to forage and breed (948 949 Gilmore et al. 1990, 1992).

Substrate: All life stages occur over bottoms areas where vegetation is generally but not strictly absent.  Bottoms can consist of sand, mud, detritus mud, or mud with shell fragments (224 657 437 582).  Substrate often supports a rich layer of various types of algae and cyanobacteria on which these fish feed (Gilmore et al. 1990, 1271).

nodes.title: Temperature
nodes.body:
Eggs: 17.4 - 27.5 C (588); >26 C (628).  Prefer 22.8 - 28.9 C (754).
Larvae/juvenile/adult: Eurythermal.  Reported range in Texas 8.8 - 34.9 C (255 651 682 561) and 5.0 - 33.5 C in Mississippi (116 224).  In the IRL system, have been collected in waters at 43 C (279).  Sheepshead minnows have been observed to be resistant to near freezing conditions, at least for short periods (Gunter and Hildebrand 1951 657).
Salinity:  A euryhaline form recorded from freshwater to hypersaline conditions in all forms.  Observations indicate a preference for salinities of 10 - 25.0 ppt and 21.0 - 30.0 ppt, being less common above this range than below (255 257 224 694 437 116 561 140), but have been found in waters ranging from 0.0 - 167 ppt (949).  The high extreme of this range is probably very close to the upper toleration limit for this species (135 321 437 255 263 588 651 657 754).

nodes.title: REPRODUCTION
nodes.body:
Reproductive Mode: Sheepshead minnows are gonochoristic, sexually dimorphic, polygamous, iteroparous, and oviparous with externally fertilized demersal eggs defended by breeding males.(306 Raney et al. 1953; Kodric-Brown 1977, 1978; Itzkowitz 1974, 1981, 1984).
Mating and Spawning:  Extended spawning season, February-October and probably year-round in warmer waters (393 306 257 378 437 611 178).  Ripe females have been collected in water temperatures ranging from 15 to 28.5  (611).  Drops in salinity may initiate spawning activity (437).  Spawning can occur at depths of 2.5 - 61 cm in shallow arms of small bays, large tide pools, mangrove lagoons, roadside ditches, and pools in shallow, gently flowing streams over bottoms of sand, black silt, or mud.  Males occupy territories up to 0.3 - 0.6 m in diameter and perform an elaborate series of behaviors to defend the territory and attract potential mates (Raney et al. 1953; Kodric-Brown 1977, 1978; Itzkowitz 1974, 1981, 1984).  During these behaviors, the males display an iridescent blue/green color (Raney et al. 1953; Kodric-Brown 1978).  They may or may not construct nest pits.  Pits, when constructed, are over sand or gravel and over soft mud bottoms having a decomposing overlay and are 10_15 cm in diameter and 2.5_3.8 cm deep and are centrally located in well groomed, oval shaped territories.  Spawning may actually take place out of both pit and territory, but not usually.  Spawning territories are typically situated adjacent to banks or up to 3 m from shore and usually associated with submerged logs or rocks.  Density of territories may approach 100 per 0.9 m^2 area (275 Raney et al. 1953 657 754).
Fecundity: Sheepshead minnows are fractional spawners.  Fecundity varies with each spawn/female.  Single females spawn a number of times during a single season at intervals of 1_7 days with an average of 4 spawnings per nest entry, and deposit 1 - 3 eggs per spawning.  The number of eggs produced over a 28 day period per female in vitro ranged from 2 - 1,028 and averaged 186.  Another study reported from 2 - 24 eggs spawned by a single female on thirty occasions from April 9, through August 16 with the possibility that the actual number may have exceeded observations.  The ovary from a single female contained 140 oocytes with at least 50% mature (178 275 306 393 628).

nodes.title: Length Range
nodes.body:
Egg: Oviparous, demersal, adhesive or semi-adhesive by means of minute threads sticking to plants, the sides of aquaria, each other, and the bottom substrate.  Eggs are spherical in form 1.0 - 1.73 mm in diameter, yellowish in color and highly translucent.  Egg membrane is thick and heavy with a perceptible perivitelline space between it and the vitelline membrane.  Small groups of minute oil globules are scattered over the surface of the yolk sphere that normally rests at the upper pole.  Incubation is from 4 - 12 d; 12 d at 17.4 - 25.5 C and 110 ppt salinity; 5 - 6 d at laboratory temperature; 5 d at 30 C; 4 - 5 d at 28 C and 30 ppt salinity.  Hatching typically observed in spring and summer (275 346 306 393 588 628).
Larvae: 4 mm TL at hatching.  Yolk relatively large; dorsal and ventral fin fold continuous.  Larvae slightly yellowish in color and posterior half of body is marked by lighter and darker vertical bands.  At five days after hatching yolk is almost completely absorbed and larvae are >5 mm TL.  General color still yellowish with vertical bands slightly more conspicuous.  At 9 mm many adult characters are apparent; vertical bands present but not fully developed.  Considered juveniles at 12 mm (306 312 393 628).
Juvenile: Back becomes strongly elevated, body depth proportionally greater, caudal fin more rounded than in adult.  Coloration quite characteristic although general color lighter in the adult.  Juveniles reach maturity in vitro at 3 mo with sex dichromatism and ripe females occurring at 27 mm (393 628).  Growth is ca. 5 mm/mo from March through October (611).
Adult: Reported averages for each sex in Texas are 45.0 mm TL for males, and 46.5 mm TL for females (657).  Collected in IRL wetlands up to 51 mm SL (1271).  Largest published size is 93 mm (255).

nodes.title: FOOD HABITS
nodes.body: Sheepshead minnows are primary consumers often termed herbivorous, detritivorous, and infrequently larvivorous and omnivorous.  Diet principally consists of plant material, diatoms and other algae, detritus, and mosquito larvae and pupae.  The remains of copepods, insects, amphipods, fish, sponge, annelid fragments, and pelecypods have also been reported.  Sand and mud are also conspicuous stomach components (312 257 657 664 279 436 515 611 628 684 554 1271).

sections.heading: HEADER
sections.content:
Title: Sheepshead minnow (Cyprinodon variegatus)

FLELMR Code:  1396

sections.heading: Revisions
sections.content:
4/4/94.  Ron E. Brockmeyer; Harbor Branch Oceanographic Institution

Common Name: Sheepshead minnow
Scientific Name: Cyprinodon variegatus

Other Common Names - Variegated minnow (306); Sheepshead killifish (279); Sheepshead pupfish (54); broad killifish, and chubby (70).

sections.heading: Classification
sections.content:
Phylum:  Chordata
	Class:  Osteichthyes
	Order:  Atheriniformes
	Family:  Cyprinodontidae

Note: A reference for Order =  (607 608)

sections.heading: VALUE & STATUS
sections.content:
Commercial:  Some commercial value as bait (657 554).  Statistics of their use are unknown as no records are kept.
Recreational: This species has no recreational value other than its use as bait by fishermen.
Indicator: Used extensively as a bioassay organism by United States Environmental Protection Agency and others for acute, partial chronic, and chronic bioassays necessary for setting water quality standards.  Testing is primarily for effects of organochlorides on the estuarine community, but recent work has indicated this species is useful in the evaluation of the hepatocarcinogenic risks of chemicals in contaminated coastal waters (148 240 629 628).
Ecological Role: The sheepshead minnow and other cyprinodontids are important in the control of salt water mosquitoes (306 279) and also in the export of energy from the marsh by serving as food for birds and larger fish (306 651 554).  It was the dominant species in both abundance and biomass found in IRL impounded wetlands (948).  Piscine predators include: Centropomus undecimalis, Morone interrupta, Cynoscion nebulosus, Micropogonias undulatus, Elops saurus, Megalops atlanticus, and Sciaenops ocellata (163 235 255 1026 1374).

sections.heading: GEOGRAPHIC RANGE
sections.content:
Overall:  Along the Atlantic coast, from Maine to Yucatan, Mexico, and throughout West Indies to northern South America (54 327 275).
Within Study Area:  Throughout Florida in shallow peripheral waters (953 848 790 581 664).

Mobility and Migration:

sections.heading: Life Mode
sections.content:
This euryhaline, oviparous, detrital-algavore feeds at the bottom in shallow open peripheral areas (279 281 953 848 790 581 664).  Markedly diurnal (Breder 1959 611); has been observed to school especially when frightened (312 437); nektonic in shallow coastal/inland waters (582  279 664 702).  Males defend breeding territories and the demersal eggs layed there (393 628 275 Kodric-Brown 1977, 1978; Raney et al. 1953).
Movements and Migrations:  Observed movements of this species appear to be influenced by seasonal fluctuations in temperature.  As temperatures begin to drop in the fall there is a general movement to warmer, slightly deeper waters.  It has been noted that at this time sheepshead minnows can be taken by trawls in these deeper waters where none were present during warmer months (70 255 657).

sections.heading: BENTHIC HABITAT
sections.content:
Habitat Type: All stages are estuarine: restricted to bays and inland areas preferring shallow bottom, quiet waters; found in salt marshes, sloughs, coves, bays, creeks, and ditches (70 224 262 263 312 437 657 682).  Larval specimens often occupy the water's edge while larger individuals (7mm) may stay on the bottom (754).  Take advantage of mosquito control practices in wetlands associated with the IRL to spread across artificially flooded high marsh habitat to forage and breed (948 949 Gilmore et al. 1990, 1992).

Substrate: All life stages occur over bottoms areas where vegetation is generally but not strictly absent.  Bottoms can consist of sand, mud, detritus mud, or mud with shell fragments (224 657 437 582).  Substrate often supports a rich layer of various types of algae and cyanobacteria on which these fish feed (Gilmore et al. 1990, 1271).

sections.heading: Temperature
sections.content:
Eggs: 17.4 - 27.5 C (588); >26 C (628).  Prefer 22.8 - 28.9 C (754).
Larvae/juvenile/adult: Eurythermal.  Reported range in Texas 8.8 - 34.9 C (255 651 682 561) and 5.0 - 33.5 C in Mississippi (116 224).  In the IRL system, have been collected in waters at 43 C (279).  Sheepshead minnows have been observed to be resistant to near freezing conditions, at least for short periods (Gunter and Hildebrand 1951 657).
Salinity:  A euryhaline form recorded from freshwater to hypersaline conditions in all forms.  Observations indicate a preference for salinities of 10 - 25.0 ppt and 21.0 - 30.0 ppt, being less common above this range than below (255 257 224 694 437 116 561 140), but have been found in waters ranging from 0.0 - 167 ppt (949).  The high extreme of this range is probably very close to the upper toleration limit for this species (135 321 437 255 263 588 651 657 754).

sections.heading: REPRODUCTION
sections.content:
Reproductive Mode: Sheepshead minnows are gonochoristic, sexually dimorphic, polygamous, iteroparous, and oviparous with externally fertilized demersal eggs defended by breeding males.(306 Raney et al. 1953; Kodric-Brown 1977, 1978; Itzkowitz 1974, 1981, 1984).
Mating and Spawning:  Extended spawning season, February-October and probably year-round in warmer waters (393 306 257 378 437 611 178).  Ripe females have been collected in water temperatures ranging from 15 to 28.5  (611).  Drops in salinity may initiate spawning activity (437).  Spawning can occur at depths of 2.5 - 61 cm in shallow arms of small bays, large tide pools, mangrove lagoons, roadside ditches, and pools in shallow, gently flowing streams over bottoms of sand, black silt, or mud.  Males occupy territories up to 0.3 - 0.6 m in diameter and perform an elaborate series of behaviors to defend the territory and attract potential mates (Raney et al. 1953; Kodric-Brown 1977, 1978; Itzkowitz 1974, 1981, 1984).  During these behaviors, the males display an iridescent blue/green color (Raney et al. 1953; Kodric-Brown 1978).  They may or may not construct nest pits.  Pits, when constructed, are over sand or gravel and over soft mud bottoms having a decomposing overlay and are 10_15 cm in diameter and 2.5_3.8 cm deep and are centrally located in well groomed, oval shaped territories.  Spawning may actually take place out of both pit and territory, but not usually.  Spawning territories are typically situated adjacent to banks or up to 3 m from shore and usually associated with submerged logs or rocks.  Density of territories may approach 100 per 0.9 m^2 area (275 Raney et al. 1953 657 754).
Fecundity: Sheepshead minnows are fractional spawners.  Fecundity varies with each spawn/female.  Single females spawn a number of times during a single season at intervals of 1_7 days with an average of 4 spawnings per nest entry, and deposit 1 - 3 eggs per spawning.  The number of eggs produced over a 28 day period per female in vitro ranged from 2 - 1,028 and averaged 186.  Another study reported from 2 - 24 eggs spawned by a single female on thirty occasions from April 9, through August 16 with the possibility that the actual number may have exceeded observations.  The ovary from a single female contained 140 oocytes with at least 50% mature (178 275 306 393 628).

sections.heading: Length Range
sections.content:
Egg: Oviparous, demersal, adhesive or semi-adhesive by means of minute threads sticking to plants, the sides of aquaria, each other, and the bottom substrate.  Eggs are spherical in form 1.0 - 1.73 mm in diameter, yellowish in color and highly translucent.  Egg membrane is thick and heavy with a perceptible perivitelline space between it and the vitelline membrane.  Small groups of minute oil globules are scattered over the surface of the yolk sphere that normally rests at the upper pole.  Incubation is from 4 - 12 d; 12 d at 17.4 - 25.5 C and 110 ppt salinity; 5 - 6 d at laboratory temperature; 5 d at 30 C; 4 - 5 d at 28 C and 30 ppt salinity.  Hatching typically observed in spring and summer (275 346 306 393 588 628).
Larvae: 4 mm TL at hatching.  Yolk relatively large; dorsal and ventral fin fold continuous.  Larvae slightly yellowish in color and posterior half of body is marked by lighter and darker vertical bands.  At five days after hatching yolk is almost completely absorbed and larvae are >5 mm TL.  General color still yellowish with vertical bands slightly more conspicuous.  At 9 mm many adult characters are apparent; vertical bands present but not fully developed.  Considered juveniles at 12 mm (306 312 393 628).
Juvenile: Back becomes strongly elevated, body depth proportionally greater, caudal fin more rounded than in adult.  Coloration quite characteristic although general color lighter in the adult.  Juveniles reach maturity in vitro at 3 mo with sex dichromatism and ripe females occurring at 27 mm (393 628).  Growth is ca. 5 mm/mo from March through October (611).
Adult: Reported averages for each sex in Texas are 45.0 mm TL for males, and 46.5 mm TL for females (657).  Collected in IRL wetlands up to 51 mm SL (1271).  Largest published size is 93 mm (255).

sections.heading: FOOD HABITS
sections.content: Sheepshead minnows are primary consumers often termed herbivorous, detritivorous, and infrequently larvivorous and omnivorous.  Diet principally consists of plant material, diatoms and other algae, detritus, and mosquito larvae and pupae.  The remains of copepods, insects, amphipods, fish, sponge, annelid fragments, and pelecypods have also been reported.  Sand and mud are also conspicuous stomach components (312 257 657 664 279 436 515 611 628 684 554 1271).
